correctness.rationale: The exact 4-point inclusion-exclusion identity and known disk baseline reduce the theorem to Q1(t) through first order and Q2(t) through zeroth. Angular density gives F(u)=1/4-6u²/pi²+o(u²); disk area integration gives M(u)=4/(9pi)+2u²/(3pi)+o(u²), so Q1(t)=3/4-4/(3pi²)+2t/pi²+o(t). Two-inner-point cone analysis gives Q2→1/2. Algebra yields the stated second coefficient. Local integrability, null boundaries and dominated convergence justify limits; checker independently verifies finite cases and algebra.

value.rationale: A centered puncture is a canonical perturbation of Sylvester’s four-point problem. The second-order coefficient has a strict negative sign, revealing a nonlinear response opposite the known positive first derivative. Its derivation combines a nontrivial fixed-point quadratic kernel with a distinct two-point collapse geometry and gives useful finite-hole correction, without asserting global concavity.
